headings.title: SMTO-EXE-0202 — SMTO couldn't read the text in your scanned PDF

html:
SMTO-EXE-0202 — SMTO couldn't read the text in your scanned PDF

GUID: 2e723a5f-67f4-5595-a1ab-de71010326a1
Slug: pdf-ocr-failed
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: pdf

What happened

  • SMTO tried to read the words on the scanned pages but the text-reading step didn't finish properly. Your original PDF was not changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask SMTO to read the text from one page or a few pages at a time instead of the whole document. This message does not establish which page was too slow, and each page has a short time limit for text reading.
  2. If you only need the words, ask for text only rather than a searchable PDF. Making a searchable PDF takes more work per page than reading the text alone.
  3. If you asked for a higher quality than the standard 144 DPI, ask again without setting a quality. Higher quality makes bigger page images, which take longer to read.
  4. If you stopped the task yourself while it was reading, this message is expected. Ask again when you're ready. Stopping a task ends the text reading partway, which also shows this message.

What success looks like

  • SMTO shows the text from the pages you chose, or a searchable PDF appears under Artifacts from this run.

If it still fails

  • If even one page fails, select Copy error details and send them, with the page number, to the person who manages SMTO. Keep the original scanned PDF unchanged.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Local Tesseract OCR on the Gateway failed for a reason other than a missing engine or language (time or output limit, unusable page image, or cancellation).

What this means

  • PDF OCR caught a shared screen/OCR failure other than missing engine/language support, including processing, input, cancellation or resource-bound errors from that path. PDF parsing and OCR remain local bounded operations on the selected Gateway. Outputs are separate create-only files/artifacts; diagnostic rendering adds no reads, credential recovery, model calls or automatic retries.

Why this can happen

  • PDF OCR caught a shared screen/OCR failure other than missing engine/language support, including processing, input, cancellation or resource-bound errors from that path.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the original OCR mode, page count, DPI and available bounded cause; this broad translation does not identify one root cause.

How to fix it

  • The worker maps every Tesseract ScreenError other than ocr_unavailable to pdf.ocr_failed and does not keep the inner kind: ocr_limit (per-page 10 s / 2 MB for text, 20 s / 32 MB for searchable PDF, within the 60 s worker budget), ocr_input (unusable page image or engine output) or screen_cancelled. Reproduce on one page at the default 144 DPI to tell a limit from bad input; no searchable PDF is staged when OCR fails, but check the run's artifacts before another searchable_pdf write.
  • Inspect the OCR operation and retained cause. Correct supported input/settings or reduce work only when the evidence calls for it; check existing outputs before another write.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect the bounded PDF receipt and input, reduce the request if needed, and retry only after resolving the reported condition.

How to verify the fix

  • A justified bounded OCR operation produces verified text or searchable output while preserving the original source.

What not to do

  • Never automatically replay uncertain writes or execute embedded document content.

Technical notes

  • PDF parsing and OCR remain local bounded operations on the selected Gateway. Outputs are separate create-only files/artifacts; diagnostic rendering adds no reads, credential recovery, model calls or automatic retries.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
